mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 1.0%) compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the monetary policy stance remains accommodative.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% within a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based demand contraction, which triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity weakens.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * RSAFS) has a negative coefficient in a regression of 60-day returns with p-value > 0.05, or the negative return rate is below 55% when both series decline.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 100 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the level of real GDP (GDPC1) exceeds 16800 billion of chained 2017 dollars, it indicates strong economic growth that supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 16800 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * UNRATE) has a positive coefficient in a regression of 20-day returns with p-value > 0.05, or the positive return rate is below 55% when both series move in the expected direction.

mechanism_narrative: In a high interest rate regime (FEDFUNDS above 2.0%), monetary policy is restrictive, which reduces corporate investment and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).
